skill.name: twitter-automation
skill.description: Automate Twitter and X account workflows through the inference.sh CLI, including posts, media posts, likes, retweets, DMs, follows, and profile lookups.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh CLI workflows for Twitter and X publishing, engagement, messaging, and profile lookup tasks.
skill.author: inference-shell

security_audit.summary: Many static findings are Markdown fences or inline app identifiers and were marked false positive for Ruby-style backtick execution. The actual infsh examples are confirmed medium-risk external commands because they authenticate, publish, delete, message, follow, or retrieve data through a connected X account. A high-confidence semantic finding remains for social engagement automation that could support spam or platform manipulation without guardrails.

remediation.issue: Social engagement workflows lack explicit abuse guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation, rate limits, recipient allowlists, and policy checks before likes, retweets, follows, DMs, deletes, or posts run.

remediation.issue: The skill allows broad inference.sh CLI execution.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed commands to the documented X app actions where possible, and add preview or dry-run steps before account-changing commands.

remediation.issue: Remote media and documentation links can fetch external content.
remediation.suggestion: Proxy or pin marketplace images, and warn users to review third-party media URLs before publishing them to X.

content.value_statement: Manual social account actions can slow approved publishing and engagement work. This skill uses inference.sh CLI apps to run Twitter and X posting, media, messaging, and profile workflows.
actual_capabilities: Posts text tweets and media posts through inference.sh X apps.
Likes, retweets, deletes, and retrieves posts by tweet ID.
Sends direct messages when a recipient ID and approved text are provided.
Follows users and retrieves user profiles by username.
Shows workflows for publishing AI-generated images and videos to X.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and a configured X integration.
Does not include built-in rate limits, consent checks, or anti-spam controls.
Examples use placeholder tweet IDs, usernames, and media URLs.
Does not verify X policy compliance or content approval before actions run.

use_cases.title: Publish Approved Updates
use_cases.description: Post prepared announcements, launch notes, or media updates from a connected X account after review.

use_cases.title: Share Developer Content
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable workflow for posting release updates, generated visuals, and profile lookups during launches.

use_cases.title: Handle Account Operations
use_cases.description: Retrieve posts, check profiles, delete mistaken posts, or send approved follow-up messages through one CLI workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Post a Basic Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Use twitter-automation to post this approved text to X: [text]. Confirm the connected account and exact text before running any command.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Media Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a media post with this text and media URL: [text], [media URL]. Show me the final post content and ask for approval before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Review Engagement Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: For these tweet IDs, plan any likes or retweets and explain the reason for each action. Ask for approval before executing any engagement.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Campaign Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a step-by-step workflow to generate media with inference.sh, publish it to X, retrieve the post, and report the result. Ask before each public action.

output_examples.input: Post an approved launch announcement to X.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms the connected account, previews the exact text, asks for approval, publishes the post, and reports the final status.

output_examples.input: Retrieve an X profile for a username.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for the username, retrieves the profile through the configured app, and summarizes the returned profile details.

output_examples.input: Create a post with approved text and a media URL.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares a media post, previews the final content, requests approval, publishes through the media app, and reports completion.

best_practices: Require explicit approval before posting, deleting, following, retweeting, liking, or sending DMs.
Verify the connected account, target IDs, usernames, and final content before running commands.
Use rate limits, audit logs, and internal policy checks for every account-changing workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for bulk follows, engagement farming, or unsolicited direct messages.
Do not run public account actions from untrusted prompts or unreviewed generated content.
Do not place secrets, credentials, or private customer data in post text or direct messages.

faq.question: What account does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the X account connected to the configured inference.sh integration and active CLI session.

faq.question: Does the skill store X credentials?
faq.answer: No credential storage is shown in the skill file. Authentication is handled by the inference.sh CLI and integration.

faq.question: Can it post media?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents media posting through the x/post-create app with a media URL.

faq.question: Can it schedule posts?
faq.answer: The description mentions scheduling, but the examples show immediate CLI actions. Use an external scheduler if needed.

faq.question: Is it safe for bulk engagement?
faq.answer: No. Bulk likes, follows, retweets, or DMs need strict consent, rate limits, and policy review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the inference.sh CLI is available.
